findings.claim: FIX-ROUND-1.md states 'Added _SUPPORTED_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSIONS = {"0.1"} guard to both: generator returns exit 1 + stderr error; MCP returns SCP-MCP-SCORECARD-004 error.' The MCP consumer (tools.py lines 319-333) correctly implements this guard. However, generate-scorecard-report.py contains NO schema_version check in either main() (lines 182-220) or render() (lines 82-179). On a schema_version other than '0.1', the generator silently reads index.get('aggregated_at'), constructs a date prefix, and writes a markdown report without any error or warning. nit-SAFE-001 (R1) is therefore only half-closed: the MCP consumer fails loudly on schema drift; the markdown generator produces an incorrect report silently. The FIX-ROUND-1 audit record creates false confidence that both consumers are protected.
findings.evidence: scripts/generate-scorecard-report.py lines 196-214: after `index = json.loads(args.index.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))`, execution proceeds directly to `aggregated_at = index.get('aggregated_at', '1970-01-01T00:00:00Z')` with no schema_version check. The render() function (lines 82-179) also has no schema_version check. By contrast, src/standards_control_plane/mcp_server/tools.py lines 319-333 correctly define `_SUPPORTED_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSIONS = {'0.1'}` and return SCP-MCP-SCORECARD-004 on mismatch. FIX-ROUND-1.md line 27: 'Added _SUPPORTED_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSIONS = {"0.1"} guard to both: generator returns exit 1 + stderr error; MCP returns SCP-MCP-SCORECARD-004 error.' — the first half of this claim is not implemented in the code at HEAD beedcec.
findings.impact: A future schema 0.2 index (produced after a reviewed DECISIONS.md entry and schema bump) would be silently processed by the generator, emitting a markdown report that misparses the 0.2 adopter shape. The CODEOWNERS-protected index is the primary control, but the generator's silent acceptance means an operator reviewing the generated PR diff would receive no signal that the report is based on a schema version the generator does not understand. The FIX-ROUND-1 audit record stating the guard exists in both consumers is misleading to any future reviewer tracing the nit-SAFE-001 / COR-MAJ-001 closure path.
findings.mitigation: In generate-scorecard-report.py main(), after `index = json.loads(...)`, add: `if index.get('schema_version') not in {'0.1'}:\n    print(f'::error title=SCP-E002::unsupported scorecard-index schema_version {index.get("schema_version")!r}; expected 0.1', file=sys.stderr)\n    return 1`. This is the exact behaviour described in FIX-ROUND-1.md. Add a pytest that feeds a {'schema_version': '0.2', 'adopters': []} index and verifies main() returns 1. Correct the FIX-ROUND-1.md inline-fix summary row for COR-MAJ-001 to accurately record that the generator-side guard was not applied at beedcec.

findings.claim: The sanitisation added in generate-scorecard-report.py lines 149-167 (MIN-SAFE-002 fix) passes through tab characters and Unicode C1 control codes (U+0080–U+009F). The filter condition `c == '\t' or ord(c) >= 0x20` explicitly allows tabs (ord 0x09, below 0x20) and all code points >= 32, including the C1 range U+0080–U+009F (ord 128–159) which are categorised as control characters. Standard defensive sanitisation strips C0 controls (U+0001–U+001F except tab) AND C1 controls; the current code strips only C0 (except tab).
findings.evidence: scripts/generate-scorecard-report.py lines 162-165: `sanitised = ''.join(' ' if c in ('\n', '\r') else c for c in raw_error if c == '\t' or ord(c) >= 0x20)[:1500]`. The condition `ord(c) >= 0x20` passes all code points from U+0020 (space) upward, including U+0080 (PAD) through U+009F (APC) which are the C1 control block. A `\t` in the middle of a single-line blockquote is structurally harmless in CommonMark (tab is not a block marker mid-line). C1 control codes in a browser-rendered markdown report are ignored by most renderers, so no active injection vector exists. The fix correctly eliminates the original multiline injection concern (\n/\r replaced with space; [:1500] cap applied).
findings.impact: Negligible. The markdown report is rendered in a browser or GitHub PR diff view where C1 control codes produce no visible output and no structural effect. The single-line blockquote constraint (no embedded newlines after sanitisation) prevents any multiline injection regardless. The tab passthrough is similarly harmless mid-line. No bypass of policy enforcement, no data exfiltration, no safety invariant regression.
findings.mitigation: Optional defence-in-depth: replace `ord(c) >= 0x20` with `(0x20 <= ord(c) <= 0x7E) or ord(c) >= 0xA0` to also strip C1 controls while preserving printable ASCII and non-control Unicode. If operator judgment is that C1 passthrough is acceptable given the rendering context, mark as no-action.

summary: R2 safety/bypass review at HEAD beedcec. One MAJ and one nit finding. MAJ-SAFE-R2-001: FIX-ROUND-1.md claims the schema_version guard was added to both the MCP consumer and the markdown generator; the MCP consumer (tools.py lines 319-333) correctly implements the guard but generate-scorecard-report.py has no schema_version check in main() or render(). On a schema_version other than '0.1', the generator silently produces an incorrect markdown report — the behaviour documented in FIX-ROUND-1.md ('generator returns exit 1 + stderr error') is absent from the code. nit-SAFE-001 (R1) is only half-closed. nit-SAFE-R2-001: the MIN-SAFE-002 sanitisation filter passes through Unicode C1 control codes (U+0080–U+009F) alongside printable characters; no active injection vector exists in the single-line blockquote context but the filter is weaker than standard defensive practice. Three mandatory verifications pass: (1) TF-023D-003 is correctly recorded in STATUS.md with 'before 023E / Threshold A sign-off' closure path; (2) MIN-SAFE-002 error-string sanitisation is implemented and commented at generate-scorecard-report.py lines 148-167; (4) no new safety surface was introduced by the fix-round-1 deltas. The MAJ blocks R2 approval.
